best_human.provenance: Charles E. Roberts reports order-12 orthogonal sets meeting the then-current lower bound. Sage's pinned database separately attributes its explicit five-square data to Brendan McKay.
best_human.evidence_state: five-square witness replayed and exactly verified; no optimality proof

best_public.evidence_state: pinned Sage 10.10 database includes a McKay-attributed order-12 family of five; no checked source establishes that five is optimal

best_reproduced.provenance: Literal digit-for-digit extraction of the MOLS_12_5 string in Sage 10.10 source, mapping a..l to 0..11. The Sage function was not executed.
best_reproduced.evidence_state: independently replayed; every Latin and orthogonality constraint checked exactly

ai_assisted.evidence_state: no higher AI-assisted construction found in the sources checked

scope_note: The five-square lower bound is not an optimality result. The general upper bound is 11. A complete family of 11 is equivalent to a projective plane of order 12, whose existence remains open. This archive does not claim that no six-square family exists.
